title: Does demand-driven simulation mislead leak detection on a stressed water network, and where does pressure-driven demand change the answer?
lede: Net3 leak signals under demand-driven and pressure-driven demand (WNTR): identical at 1 to 1.25 times base demand and nearly so at 1.5 times; beyond that both models fail because the pumps cannot meet demand (simulated; one network).
summary: WNTR simulates EPANET’s Net3 for 72 hours at demand multipliers 1 to 3 under the default demand-driven model and the pressure-driven model (required pressure 15 m, 10 and 25 m swept), with a leak of 2 % of mean demand at 30 seeded junctions read at five sensors. At 1 and 1.25 times base demand the two models agree to the three decimals printed; at 1.5 times the median sensor drop is 0.798 m against 0.792 m and 29 of 30 locations are seen by both. At 2 and 3 times the pumps run past their rated flow, the demand-driven run has 60–91 % of junction-hours below 0 m (down to −458 m) and the leak passes no flow, while the pressure-driven run serves 86 % and 62 % of demand and still sits below the required pressure over half the time, so neither is believable there. Hence the conclusions of the earlier detector study, drawn at base demand, do not depend on the demand model. Limits: one textbook network whose low-pressure nodes are mostly zero-demand, noise-free sensor response only (no detectors or false-alarm budget), assumed required pressure, 30 locations and one leak size.
